senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: the quality of holiness as an expression of the divine in contrast with the human
generic word for a large bird of prey; genus Aquila, but may include others, esp. vulture
senses.comment: In Revelation 12:14 the emphasis is upon strength and speed, and therefore a term meaning ‘eagle’ is probably more satisfactory, but in Matthew 24:28 (and the parallel passages in Luke 17:37) the reference is to the eating of dead flesh, and therefore a word meaning ‘vultures’ is more appropriate.|The basic distinction between eagles and vultures is that the former either capture their prey or feed upon dead carcasses, while vultures only feed upon dead carcasses. Only in the Western Hemisphere are there two distinct families of birds: (1) birds of prey, which also feed upon dead bodies (eagles) and (2) vultures, which never take live prey, but only feed upon carcasses.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: pertaining to the lack of a favorable opportunity for doing something
glosses: when the time is not right

senses.def: a position other than the one in the immediate context
the totality of two
senses.comment: In a number of languages ἀμφότεροι may be rendered as ‘the two.’

senses.def: all of a few (three or more)
senses.comment: It is clear that in Acts 19:16 ἀμφότεροι must refer to the seven sons of a Jewish high priest named Sceva.

senses.def: to move back to a point or area from which one has previously departed, but with more explicit emphasis upon the return (compare ὑποστρέφω[a], 15.88)
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἀναλύω to depart, not occurring in the NT) to depart from life, as a euphemistic expression for death
pertaining to having no reason or need for being ashamed or feeling disgrace
a recompense based upon what one deserves, either positive or negative, but with special emphasis upon the reciprocal nature of the recompense
to take off or strip off clothing
to destroy or to cause the destruction of persons, objects, or institutions
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is difficult to find a general term for ‘destruction.’ What has often happened is the extension of meaning from a more specific type of reference, for example, ‘to smash,’ to a more generic meaning of ‘to destroy,’ and whether one understands the specific or more generic meaning depends largely upon the context. Accordingly, in Acts 8:3 one may find a figurative usage of a term meaning ‘to smash’ (though understood in a more generic sense), for example, ‘Saul then worked in order to smash the church.’

senses.def: to fail to obtain a valued object
to lose something which one already possesses
senses.comment: ἀπόλλυμι in the sense of losing what one already possesses may be analyzed basically as ‘not to have that which one has previously had.’ There is, however, no suggestion in ἀπόλλυμι[c] as to the particular type of circumstances involved in the loss, whether, for example, from neglect, by accident, or as the result of some external force.|It is also possible to interpret ἀπόλλυμι in Luke 15:8 as ‘to not know where something is’ (see 27.29).

senses.def: to become unaware of the location of something
glosses: to no longer know where something is
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret ἀπόλλυμι in Luke 15:4 as meaning a loss of possession (see 57.68)

senses.def: an idiom, literally: to suffer the destruction of one’s life, or: to have one’s life destroyed
glosses: to experience the loss of life
senses.comment: In Matthew 10:39 some scholars see in the use of ψυχή a reference not to physical life but to a particular quality of life. This is difficult to justify except in terms of the total context, and it may be that in Matthew 10:39 there is a degree of intentional ambiguity with respect to the meaning of ψυχή.

senses.def: to die, with the implication of ruin and destruction
senses.comment: It is possible to understand ἀπόλλυμαι in Luke 15:17 as involving a measure of exaggeration.

senses.def: to cease to exist, with a possible implication of violent means
to be lost, in the religious or spiritual sense
probably a reference to the Sinai Peninsula
a principal priest, in view of belonging to one of the high-priestly families
senses.comment: In a number of languages ‘chief priests’ are referred to simply as ‘big priests’ or ‘important priests.’

senses.def: the principal member among the chief priests

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to refuse to be engaged in the efforts of work
senses.comment: Traditional translations have often interpreted ἀτακτέω in an etymological sense of ‘not being ordered’ and hence with a meaning of ‘to behave in a disorderly manner,’ but this is quite contrary to the context.

senses.subdomain: Events Involving Liquids and Dry Masses
senses.def: to cause or to produce the foaming up of a liquid (restricted in the NT to the foaming at the mouth of a person experiencing an epileptic seizure)
senses.comment: Since foaming at the mouth is so characteristic of epileptic seizures, there should be no difficulty in finding a rather specific term to identify this type of event.

senses.def: to bewitch a person, frequently by use of the evil eye and with evil intent
senses.comment: βασκαίνω[a] differs from μαγεύω to practice magic (53.96) in that the former involves the use of so-called black magic, but for a different interpretation of βασκαίνω in Galatians 3:1, see 88.159.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to deceive a person by devious and crafty means, with the possibility of a religious connotation in view of the literal meaning ‘to bewitch’ (see 53.98)
senses.comment: It is also possible that βασκαίνω in Galatians 3:1 is to be understood literally in the sense of bewitching by means of black magic (see 53.98).

senses.def: a nickname given by Jesus to the sons of Zebedee
a district in the northern part of Palestine
the Lake of Galilee, also called Tiberias and Gennesaret
a city located at the southern part of the Dead Sea and destroyed because of its evil
cardinal number, where there are eighteen instances of a countable entity
to divide and distribute to persons on the basis of certain implied distinctions or differences
senses.comment: In 1 Corinthians 12:4 it is also possible to interpret διαίρεσις as meaning ‘difference’ or ‘variety’ (see 58.39).

senses.def: a state of difference in the nature of objects or events, with the implication of significant variety
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret διαίρεσις in 1 Corinthians 12:4 as the allotment or apportionment of such spiritual gifts (see 57.91).

senses.def: pertaining to possessing such physical properties as can be seen through
cardinal number, where there are two thousand instances of a countable entity
twelfth in a series involving either time, space, or set

senses.subdomain: Appearance as an Outward Manifestation of Form
senses.def: appearance as the form of that which is seen
senses.comment: One may also translate this expression in Luke 9:29 as ‘while he was praying, his face became different’ or ‘… his face was seen as different’ or ‘… he didn’t look the same.’

senses.def: seeing
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret εἶδος in 2 Corinthians 5:7 as meaning ‘what is seen’ (see 24.2).

senses.def: a position relatively far from the speaker, writer, or viewpoint person
to flee from or out of
to become safe from danger by avoiding or escaping
senses.comment: The meaning of this part of Romans 2:3 is ‘to become free from the danger of being judged by God.’ ἵνα κατισχύσητε ἐκφυγεῖν ταῦτα πάντα τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι ‘in order that you may be able to escape all of these things that are going to happen’ Luke 21:36. In Romans 2:3 and Luke 21:36 ἐκφεύγω should not be understood in the literal sense of running away from (see 15.63). The meaning is simply not to become involved in such danger.

senses.def: to state something with sternness
to exhibit irritation or even anger in expressing a harsh reproof
to have an intense, strong feeling of concern, often with the implication of indignation
to be engaged in some activity or function, with possible focus upon the energy or force involved

senses.subdomain: Hold a Wrong View, Be Mistaken
senses.def: to cause someone to have misleading or erroneous views concerning the truth
to rise up in open defiance of authority, with the presumed intention to overthrow it or to act in complete opposition to its demands
to be in a place on something
to press or push against
to possess power or sanction
senses.comment: In some languages the concept of ‘being in force’ may be expressed simply as ‘to work’ or ‘to do what they are supposed to do’ or ‘to be in control.’ For another interpretation of ἐπίκειμαι in Hebrews 9:10, see 13.73.

senses.def: to keep on doing something with presumed insistence
to exist, with the implication of having been established and thus having continuity and purpose
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἐπίκειμαι in Hebrews 9:10, see 76.17.

senses.def: pertaining to being needed or necessary for some particular purpose
(an idiom, literally: to be at an extreme) to be very sick, with the implication of imminent death
pertaining to the exertion of tight control

senses.subdomain: Be Eager, Be Earnest, In a Devoted Manner
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: to boil in the spirit) to show great eagerness toward something
senses.comment: In some languages it may be difficult to find an appropriate equivalent of the phrase ‘with great enthusiasm,’ but in some instances an equivalent expression may be ‘he showed how much he liked to do’ or ‘he showed how he did so with all his heart.’

senses.def: a lack of attaining a desirable state or condition
(figurative extension of meaning of term meaning literally ‘to hunt,’ ‘to trap,’ not occurring in the NT) to acquire information about an error or fault, with the purpose of causing harm or trouble
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is possible to retain the figurative meaning of ‘trap’ or ‘catch,’ but in a number of instances other figures are used, for example, ‘to cause to trip,’ ‘to cause to fall,’ ‘to hear wrong words from his mouth,’ or ‘to use his words against him.’

senses.def: the role of being a priest
the patriarch Jacob
the nation of Israel
a figurative reference to Christians as the true Israel

senses.subdomain: Up To, As Much As, To the Degree That [Marked Extent of Degree]
senses.def: in accordance with a degree as specified by the context
senses.comment: There may be a number of problems of restructuring in rendering the relationship between clauses marked by καθό[b], καθώς[a], and καθότι[b]. For example, in the case of 1 Peter 4:13 it may be necessary to translate ‘how much you share Christ’s sufferings is how much you can rejoice.’

senses.def: a marker of cause or reason, often with the implication of some implied comparison
a marker of similarity in events and states, with the possible implication of something being in accordance with something else

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a marker of a point of time which is simultaneous to or overlaps with another point of time
a marker of an event indicating how something took place
extension to a goal, normally down
senses.comment: In going from Jerusalem to Jericho (Luke 10:32), the movement would be downhill.

senses.def: extension along a path or road, implying movement
extension in every direction throughout an area

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: the position of an object oriented toward a particular direction
senses.comment: For κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω as an idiom (Philippians 3:14), see 89.56.

senses.def: a variety of positions distributed throughout an area or among a number of objects

senses.subdomain: Opposite, Over Against, Across From, Offshore From
senses.def: a position directly opposite and implying some space between

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a marker of a point of time which is simultaneous to or overlaps with another point of time

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: a marker of a point of time which is approximately simultaneous to another point of time
(with the genitive) a marker of a supernatural person or force called upon to guarantee the carrying out of an oath or vow
senses.comment: Depending upon the context, it may be necessary to be quite specific in some languages in marking the relations between swearing and the supernatural power invoked to guarantee the fulfillment of an oath. For example, in swearing that something is true, it may be necessary to translate ‘I swear that this is true and call upon God to punish me if it is not true,’ or if the swearing involves a promise, then one may translate ‘I promise to do this, but if I do not, may God punish me.’

senses.def: (with the genitive) a marker of opposition, with the possible implication of antagonism
a marker of a relation involving similarity of process
a marker of distributive relations, whether of place, time, or number
a marker of a specific element bearing a relation to something else
a marker of association, involving common, cultural, or ethnic elements
glosses: among (but often expressed by so-called possessive forms)

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: according to truth) pertaining to being a real or actual event or state
(an idiom, literally: according to that which is private) pertaining to what occurs in a private context or setting, in the sense of not being made known publicly

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: (idioms, literally: according to eyes, and: according to face) a position in front of an object, with the implication of direct sight
(an idiom, literally: according to depth) an extreme point on a scale of extent
(an idiom, literally: to have down on the head) to wear a covering over one’s head
(an idiom, literally: to accept in accordance with a charge) to accept a complaint against someone for a legal review
glosses: to accept a complaint in court
to admit a complaint to judgment
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand the expression κατὰ λόγον ἀνέχομαι in Acts 18:14 not as an idiom, but as meaning ‘to be reasonably patient with.’ See 25.171 and 89.18.

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: in accordance with a part) pertaining to an activity which proceeds part by part
(an idiom, literally: throughout only places) the only item of a class in a place

senses.subdomain: In Front Of, Face To Face, In Back Of, Behind
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: according to face) the position of one person facing another, with or without the implication of opposition
(an idiom, literally: to pursue to a goal, to press toward a goal) to strive energetically for some purpose
glosses: to press on with the purpose of

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: those things according to the face) that which seems to be so
to give very careful consideration to some matter
senses.comment: For another interpretation of κατανοέω in Romans 4:19, see 32.12.

senses.subdomain: To Think About, with the Implied Purpose of Responding Appropriately
senses.def: to give proper and decisive thought about something
senses.comment: It is also possible that κατανοέω in Acts 27:39 means simply ‘to notice’ (see 24.51), but there seems to be more involved than mere seeing.

senses.def: to come to a clear and definite understanding of something
senses.comment: For another interpretation of κατανοέω in Romans 4:19, see 30.4.

senses.def: to discover something through direct observation, with the implication of also thinking about it
senses.comment: For another interpretation of κατανοέω in Acts 27:39, see 30.43.

senses.def: to use sudden physical force against someone as the outgrowth of a hostile attitude
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘to attack’ is simply ‘to start fighting against.’ In some languages, however, the equivalent is ‘to jump on’ or ‘to grab to do harm to.’

senses.def: one who takes care of a garden or orchard
an association involving close mutual relations and involvement
to share one’s possessions, with the implication of some kind of joint participation and mutual interest
(derivative of κοινωνέω[a] ‘to share,’ 57.98) that which is readily shared
to shout or cry out, with the possible implication of the unpleasant nature of the sound
a relatively unimportant population center (in contrast with πόλις[b] ‘city,’ 1.89)

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: the inhabitants of a village
senses.comment: Though in English it may seem perfectly appropriate to speak of ‘announcing the good news to a town’ or ‘… a village,’ in a number of languages this is simply not possible, for any announcement of good news must be directed to people and not to a place or area.

senses.def: generalized, positive degree
pertaining to being useless on the basis of being futile and lacking in content
(derivative of μεστός[a] ‘very full,’ 59.39) to cause a space to be exceptionally full
senses.comment: In many instances one cannot speak of persons being ‘full of new wine.’ It is, however, possible in Acts 2:13 to say ‘they have drunk a great deal of new wine.’

senses.def: pertaining to a particularly limited quantity
a small size, relative to the norm for the class of objects in question
a very low point on a scale of extent
senses.comment: In Revelation 3:8 it would seem that μικρός might very well be classified as indicating quantity (see 59.15), but it is probably better understood as indicating the extent of a state of being powerful, expressed in a number of languages in a negative form, for example, ‘you are not very powerful.’

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a relatively brief extent of time
pertaining to being short, in a horizontal or vertical dimension

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: pertaining to a living being who is relatively young, often the younger of two objects
senses.comment: It is possible, however, that μικρός in Mark 15:40 denotes small size rather than being younger (see 81.13).

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: pertaining to being of low or unimportant status (in contrast with μέγας[d] great; important; 87.22)

senses.subdomain: Duration of Time without Reference to Points or Units of Time: Time, Spend Time, Always, Eternal, Old, Immediately, Young
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: little, how much, how much) a relatively short time, with emphasis upon the certainty of the brief period

senses.subdomain: Not Able To Be Known, Secret
senses.def: the content of that which has not been known before but which has been revealed to an in-group or restricted constituency
senses.comment: There is a serious problem involved in translating μυστήριον by a word which is equivalent to the English expression ‘mystery,’ for this term in English refers to a secret which people have tried to uncover but which they have failed to understand. In many instances μυστήριον is translated by a phrase meaning ‘that which was not known before,’ with the implication of its being revealed at least to some persons.

senses.def: to win a victory over
to guide or to direct, with the implication of making certain that people reach an appropriate destination
(a figurative extension of meaning of ὁδηγέω[a] ‘to lead, to guide,’ 15.182) to guide someone in acquiring information
a heavy rain, either in length of occurrence or in force, as in the case of a thunderstorm (thus differing from ὑετός[b], βροχή and βρέχω[a] in 14.10)
senses.comment: In some languages a rainstorm is simply ‘a rain with wind,’ but it may also be expressed as ‘rain that hurts’ or ‘rain that floods.’

senses.def: to give accurate instruction
to be under obligation to make a payment as the result of having previously received something of value
to be necessary or indispensable, with the implication of a contingency
to be obligatory in view of some moral or legal requirement

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to commit a sin against someone and thus to incur moral debt
a relatively short narrative with symbolic meaning
senses.comment: In almost all languages there is some way of speaking about parables or allegories. The equivalent in some languages may be ‘a likeness story’ or ‘a story that teaches’ or ‘a story that points the way’ or ‘words that have another meaning’ or ‘words that are saying something else important.’|Some scholars have insisted that in the NT παραβολή is used only in the sense of a story with one level of symbolic meaning, but in some contexts παραβολή is also used to identify allegories in which each element of the account has a symbolic significance. It is therefore extremely difficult to make a rigid distinction between parables and allegories.

senses.def: a model or example which anticipates or precedes a later realization
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be difficult to find a lexical item equivalent to ‘symbol,’ but one can often employ a relatively close paraphrase. For example, in referring to certain aspects of the tabernacle as being a παραβολή, one may render the first clause of Hebrews 9:9 as ‘this says something to us about the present time.’ In other languages one may sometimes use a term which means ‘picture,’ for example, ‘this is a picture for the present time’ or ‘this contains some meaning for the present time.’

senses.def: an idiom, literally: to place alongside a parable
pertaining to expressions which are not to be understood literally, but symbolically or figuratively
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be more satisfactory to translate ἐν παραβολῇ and πνευματικῶς[c] by a negative expression, for example, ‘not literally’ or ‘not really.’ The expression in Revelation 11:8 might be translated as ‘that city might be called Sodom, but it isn’t really Sodom.’

senses.def: refers to two members of the large cat family: Panthera pardus - leopard; about 2 m in length and yellowish brown with black spots arranged in rosettes all over the body and tail; hunts by stalking prey; and Acinonyx jubatus - cheetah; spotted but are slightly smaller and have longer legs than leopards; extremely fast; symbol of violent danger or of speed (cheetah)
senses.comment: As in the case of the term for ‘bear’ (4.12), this reference to a leopard occurs in the NT only in Revelation 13:2 and is likewise used as a means of describing the apocalyptic beast. A term referring to a local type of leopard or jaguar would be perfectly appropriate, and in some languages a term referring to a mountain lion has been employed. In other instances the equivalent expression is based upon a phrase meaning ‘fierce, large, cat-like animal.’ A borrowed term may also be employed with a descriptive classifier, for example, ‘an animal called leopard.’

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: (derivative of πεζός ‘on foot,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to travel by foot overland
senses.comment: In some languages a more appropriate might be ‘followed him by walking.’

senses.def: pertaining to being a special or a distinctive possession of someone
senses.comment: For another interpretation of περιούσιος in Titus 2:14, see 58.48.

senses.def: pertaining to that which is peculiar or special about some entity
senses.comment: For another interpretation of περιούσιος in Titus 2:14, see 57.5.

senses.def: that which is completely believable
glosses: that which is worthy of belief

senses.def: to believe to the extent of complete trust and reliance
senses.comment: In rendering πιστεύω[b] and πίστις[b] it would be wrong to select a term which would mean merely ‘reliance’ or ‘dependency’ or even ‘confidence,’ for there should also be a significant measure of ‘belief,’ since real trust, confidence, and reliance can only be placed in someone who is believed to have the qualities attributed to such a person.

senses.def: the state of being someone in whom complete confidence can be placed
to believe in the good news about Jesus Christ and to become a follower
(semantic derivative of πίστις[d] ‘to be a believer, Christian faith,’ 31.102) the content of what Christians believe
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret πίστις in Jude 1:3 and Galatians 1:23 as the act of believing and placing confidence in Jesus Christ (see 31.102).

senses.def: a promise or pledge of faithfulness and loyalty
to engage in open warfare
(figurative extension of meaning of πολεμέω[a] ‘to wage war,’ 55.5) to engage in serious and protracted conflict, often involving a series of attacks

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of πρασιά ‘garden plot,’ not occurring in the NT) a group of persons arranged in an orderly fashion
senses.comment: A comparison of πρασιαὶ πρασιαί in Mark 6:40 with συμπόσια συμπόσια (see 11.5) in Mark 6:39 indicates clearly that the reference in both instances is essentially the same, but in Mark 6:39 συμπόσια συμπόσια points to the grouping of people with the intent of eating, while in Mark 6:40 πρασιαὶ πρασιαί marks the orderly arrangement of the persons. One may therefore translate Mark 6:40 as ‘the people sat down in orderly groups of a hundred and of fifty’ or ‘the people sat down in rows by groups of a hundred and groups of fifty.’

senses.def: to speak beforehand or in advance
to say in advance what is going to happen
to tell someone that some future happening is dangerous and may lead to serious consequences

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to feel strong irritation because of what someone has done

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: the watery fluid in the mouth
pertaining to what is spoken or has been spoken
a city in western Asia Minor
(a diminutive form of σῖτος ‘grain,’ 3.41, but not diminutive in meaning) any grain, but with the evident implication of its relevance as food
senses.comment: (See also 5.2.) On the basis of this one NT occurrence it is impossible to know whether the meaning of σιτία is ‘grain’ or ‘food,’ since in the phrase σιτία καὶ ποτά ‘food and drink’ (an expression occurring in a number of extrabiblical contexts), the term σιτίον contrasts solid with liquid nourishment.

senses.def: (diminutive of σῖτος[a] ‘wheat, grain,’ 3.41, but without diminutive meaning and occurring primarily in the plural) food consisting principally of grain products
senses.comment: It is, of course, possible in Acts 7:12 to understand the plural form as ‘grain’ (see 3.42), but the reference is probably to food made from grain, a common meaning of this term in Classical Greek.

senses.def: to wrap a child in swaddling clothes (long strips of cloth)
glosses: to clothe in strips of cloth
to wrap up in strips of cloth

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: pertaining to the philosophical system of the Greek philosopher Zeno, who taught that people should be free from excessive joy or grief and submit without complaint to necessity
glosses: one who adheres to Stoic philosophy
senses.comment: For comments on some translational problems, see 11.96.

senses.def: a broad, heavy tree reaching a height of some fifteen meters (about fifty feet), with large, strong branches growing out from the trunk low down on the tree; fruit has the appearance of a small fig but its taste is relatively unpleasant
senses.comment: As in the case of other specific trees for which no local term in the receptor language is available, one can borrow a word such as ‘sycamore’ from a dominant language in the area and add a classifier, for example, ‘tree called sycamore,’ but in a number of languages it may be appropriate to render συκομορέα in Luke 19:4 simply as ‘a big tree’ or ‘a wild fig tree.’

senses.def: to reestablish proper friendly interpersonal relations after these have been disrupted or broken (the componential features of this series of meanings involve (1) disruption of friendly relations because of (2) presumed or real provocation (3) overt behavior designed to remove hostility, and (4) restoration of original friendly relations)
glosses: to make things right with one another
senses.comment: Because of the variety and complexity of the components involved in reconciliation, it is often necessary to use an entire phrase in order to communicate satisfactorily the meanings of the terms in this subdomain. In some languages, however, reconciliation is often spoken of in idiomatic terms, for example, ‘to cause to become friends again,’ ‘to cause to snap fingers again’ (a symbol of friendly interpersonal relations in many parts of Africa), ‘to cause to be one again,’ or ‘to take away the separation.’ A particularly crucial element in terms for reconciliation is the assigning of responsibility for original guilt in causing the estrangement. Some terms, for example, imply that the individual who initiates reconciliation is by doing so admitting his guilt in causing the estrangement. This, of course, provides a completely untenable meaning for reconciliation in speaking of God reconciling people to himself through Christ.|In a number of languages the contextual basis for an expression for reconciliation is often found in terms relating to the reconciliation of husbands and wives. Such expressions fit in well with many contexts in the Scriptures, especially in speaking of reconciliation of people to God, since God is frequently referred to as the husband and the believers as the wife.|This is the only instance of συναλλάσσω in the NT, and it has εἰς εἰρήνην added to emphasize peace as the goal, although the feature of making peace between previously hostile individuals is already implicit in the act of reconciliation.

senses.def: to come together quickly to form a crowd
(a figurative extension of meaning of συντρέχω ‘to run with,’ not occurring in the NT) to be closely associated with others in a particular type of behavior or conduct
a proper and correct order
pertaining to having four equal sides and four right angles
cardinal number, where there are thirty instances of a countable entity
to formally and legally declare that someone who is not one’s own child is henceforth to be treated and cared for as one’s own child, including complete rights of inheritance
senses.comment: In a number of languages adoption is spoken of as ‘making a child a son’ or ‘causing a child to become a daughter.’ In some instances the equivalent expression is merely ‘to treat someone as a son’ or ‘… daughter.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to give an impression of having certain purposes or motivations, while in reality having quite different ones
senses.comment: In a number of languages ὑποκρίνομαι and ὑπόκρισις are expressed in idiomatic ways, for example, ‘to have two faces,’ ‘to have two tongues,’ ‘to be two people,’ or ‘to have two hearts.’

senses.def: information concerning a person or an event
(derivative of φόβος[a] ‘fear,’ 25.251) an object, event, or condition which causes fear
(derivative of Χαλδαία ‘Chaldea,’ not occurring in the NT) a person who is a native of Chaldea
a person who is in debt
a small piece or bit of bread
senses.comment: In John 13:26 it may be necessary to use a phrase such as ‘a broken-off piece of bread’; otherwise the inference might be that the ψωμίον was simply a scrap or crumb of bread. In some languages the appropriate equivalent of ψωμίον in this type of context is ‘a bite of bread.’
